issues.legal_issue: The holder of an impartible estate may dispose of its properties by gift or will, even if a will defeats junior family members’ right of survivorship, unless a contrary family custom or condition of tenure is established.
material_facts: The estate was impartible and subject to primogeniture.
The former holder made a gift of estate properties and bequeathed other properties by will to family members.
The successor challenged the dispositions on the ground that the holder lacked power to alienate the estate.
issues.conclusion: The holder had power to alienate the estate by both gift and will, and the will could defeat the junior family members’ right of survivorship. The challenged dispositions were valid, subject to any contrary family custom or condition of tenure being proved.
issues.legal_principle: Impartibility is a creature of custom. Under Shiba Prasad Singh v. Rani Prayag Kumari Debi, AIR 1932 PC 216, an impartible estate retains the right of survivorship but, in other respects, is clothed with incidents of self-acquired and separate property; restraint on alienation is incompatible with impartibility unless supported by custom or tenure. Rani Sartaj Kuari v. Deoraj Kuari, 15 IA 51, recognised the holder’s power of alienation, and Sri Raja Rao v. Venkata Kumari, 26 IA 83, established that a disposition by will may take priority over succession by survivorship. Protap Chandra Deo v. Jagdish Chandra Deo, 54 IA 289, and Mirza Raja Shri Pushavathi Viziaram Gajapathi Raj Manne Sultan Bahadur v. Shri Pushavathi Visweswar Gajapathi Raj, [1964] 2 SCR 403, affirmed that the power is subject to a proved contrary family custom or condition of tenure; Bhaiya Ramanuj Pratap Deo v. Lalu Maheshanuj Pratap Deo, [1982] 1 SCR 417, reiterated that principle. The Court distinguished rules governing ordinary coparcenary property, including those discussed in Chinnathayi v. Kulasekara Pandiya Naicker, [1952] SCR 241, and Seth Lakhmi Chand v. Mt. Anandi, AIR 1926 PC 54.

rule.if: challenge_to_disposition_of_impartible_estate and estate_is_impartible and holder_makes_gift_or_will and no_proven_custom_or_tenure_restriction

predicates.challenge_to_disposition_of_impartible_e: A party challenges the validity of a disposition of property comprised in an impartible estate.
predicates.estate_is_impartible: The estate is governed by a custom or tenure that makes it impartible.
predicates.holder_makes_gift_or_will: The holder of the impartible estate disposes of estate property by gift or will.
predicates.no_proven_custom_or_tenure_restriction: No family custom or condition of tenure restricting the holder’s power of alienation is established.

issues.definition: When a disposition of an impartible estate is challenged, the estate is impartible, its holder made a gift or will, and no contrary custom or tenure restriction is established, the holder may alienate the estate.

issues.legal_issue: A family custom restricting alienation of an impartible estate must be proved by positive evidence; the absence of earlier alienations or correspondence concerning only the amount of maintenance does not establish that custom.
material_facts: The challenger relied on correspondence concerning a proposed grant of maintenance to a younger family member; the correspondence addressed the amount of the grant in relation to the estate’s revenue.
The challenger also relied on the absence of an earlier instance of alienation.
The evidence did not positively establish a family custom prohibiting alienation.
issues.conclusion: The alleged family custom of inalienability was not proved.
issues.legal_principle: A party asserting a custom that restricts the holder’s power to alienate an impartible estate must produce positive evidence of that custom. Under Protap Chandra Deo v. Jagdish Chandra Deo, 54 IA 289, the mere absence of earlier instances of alienation is not sufficient evidence. Correspondence addressing only the propriety or amount of a maintenance grant does not establish a custom of inalienability.

predicates.challenge_to_custom_in_estate_dispositio: A party challenges an estate disposition and relies on a claimed family custom restricting alienation.
predicates.restrictive_family_custom_is_alleged: A party asserts that a family custom prohibits the holder from alienating the estate.
predicates.positive_evidence_of_restrictive_custom: Evidence affirmatively demonstrates a family custom prohibiting alienation, rather than merely showing no prior alienations or discussing maintenance amounts.

issues.definition: When a party challenges an estate disposition by alleging a restrictive family custom but positive evidence of that custom is absent, the custom is not established.
